title: Compassion
definition: Compassion is the Christlike movement of the heart toward the suffering, needy, weak, or lost, resulting in mercy and action.
summary: Compassion sees need and responds with mercy.
christFocus: Jesus was moved with compassion toward the sick, hungry, grieving, harassed, and lost.

studySections.heading: Doctrine in Summary
studySections.content:
Compassion is not pity from a distance. It is a mercy-filled response to real need. In Scripture, compassion often moves toward action: feeding, healing, teaching, comforting, protecting, and helping.

Jesus is full of compassion. He saw the crowds as harassed and helpless, healed the sick, fed the hungry, and welcomed the burdened.

Believers are called to put on compassionate hearts. Compassion should be guided by truth and wisdom, but it must not become cold or inactive.

studySections.heading: Why This Matters
studySections.content: Many people see suffering and look away. Compassion matters because it reflects the heart of Christ and turns concern into faithful care.

studySections.heading: Discipleship and Application
studySections.content: Ask God to make you attentive to suffering. Move toward people with mercy, listen well, and take practical action where you can help.
